newsitem.title: USA: Chrysler loses minivan production in St. Louis.
newsitem.headline: Chrysler loses minivan production in St. Louis.

text.p: Chrysler Corp. said Friday it lost about two hours of production at its St. Louis South minivan assembly plant Thursday morning when several hundred hourly workers called in sick.
The workers from United Auto Worker Local 110 were protesting the layoff of about 100 workers from the plant, Chrysler spokesman Tony Cervone said Friday.

The laid off workers had been on temporary assignment at the facility in Fenton, Mo. They were assigned to work installing trim as part of the launch of Chrysler's redesigned minivan in the spring of 1995.

It is standard procedure for Chrysler to start production of a new model with more workers than it will eventually need to produce the vehicle on a long-term basis, Cervone said. As permanent UAW Chrysler workers, the people who finished their temporary assignments will continue to receive nearly all of their regular pay until they are assigned to a new facility.
A representative from UAW Local 110 was not available for comment.

Chrysler said earlier this week it will add production of 9,000 Ram pickup trucks at the nearby St. Louis North plant for the 1997 model year, Cervone said. Previous plans called for the plant to make about 110,000 of the pickups.
"It is likely that some of those people will find a home across the street," he said.
Chrysler also plans to build an additional 25,000 trucks at St. Louis North plant in the 1998 model year.
Chrysler's stock fell 12.5 cents to $28 on the New York Stock Exchange.
